messages.subject: Re: Error when i execute rattle()
messages.body_plain:
On 3/28/2016 9:07 PM, Sujith Shivaprakash wrote:
> Whenever I execute rattle(), the GUI loads however, the R console
> gives the following error:
> Error in loadNamespace(name) : there is no package called ‘stringr’

> --

> Groups "rattle-users" group.

> an email to rattle-users...@googlegroups.com

> <mailto:rattle-users...@googlegroups.com>.

> To post to this group, send email to rattle...@googlegroups.com

> <mailto:rattle...@googlegroups.com>.

> Visit this group at https://groups.google.com/group/rattle-users.
> For more options, visit https://groups.google.com/d/optout.

The error message says that it cannot find the 'stringr' package which
rattle depends on.  So, you need to install the 'stringr' package (which
you can get from CRAN).

Dan

Daniel Nordlund
Bothell, WA  USA

messages.body_plain:

option to extract the score (pseudo-probability) for each observation?
All I’m aware of is getting the actual predicted classification (yes
or no).
   I want to demonstrate where the ROC curve comes from, and how to use
a cutoff other than 50%.

Thanks!

messages.subject: Problem loading data into Rattle 4.1.0
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I installed Rattle on my Mac running on OS X 10.11.4 (El Capitan). I can open it and browse through its menus, but when I try to load a file (e.g. a csv file; however I also tried an RData file - no difference) I get an error message that says

"dispatchExecuteButton' called by an unknown Tab" (am translating this from German system message so English original wording may differ somewhat).

Without being able to load data, I cannot use Rattle in any way. I attach the output of rattleInfo() (as the error dialogue box recommends) below in the hope that someone more in tune with these things can suggest a remedy.

Rattle looks great and I would love to use it!

Thanks and best wishes,

messages.subject: Re: Problem loading data into Rattle 4.1.0
messages.body_plain:
As per http://rattle.togaware.com/rattle-install-troubleshooting.html the problem is often solved with the following:

> Sys.setenv(LANGUAGE="en")
> library(rattle)
> rattle()

Regards,
Graham
